{"evidence":[{"sentence_id":0,"text":"Thutmose III (sometimes read as Thutmosis or Tuthmosis III, Thothmes in older history works, and meaning \"Thoth is born\") was the sixth Pharaoh of the Eighteenth Dynasty.","title":"Thutmose III"},{"sentence_id":1,"text":" During the first 22 years of Thutmose's reign he was co-regent with his stepmother and aunt, Hatshepsut, who was named the pharaoh.","title":"Thutmose III"},{"sentence_id":2,"text":" While he was shown first on surviving monuments, both were assigned the usual royal names and insignia and neither is given any obvious seniority over the other.","title":"Thutmose III"},{"sentence_id":3,"text":" He served as the head of her armies.","title":"Thutmose III"},{"sentence_id":0,"text":"Seqenenre Tao, (also Seqenera Djehuty-aa or Sekenenra Taa), called \"The Brave\", ruled over the last of the local kingdoms of the Theban region of Egypt in the Seventeenth Dynasty during the Second Intermediate Period.","title":"Seqenenre Tao"},{"sentence_id":1,"text":" He probably was the son and successor to Senakhtenre Ahmose and Queen Tetisheri.","title":"Seqenenre Tao"},{"sentence_id":2,"text":" The dates of his reign are uncertain, but he may have risen to power in the decade ending in 1560 BC or in 1558 BC (based on the probable accession date of Ahmose I, the first ruler of the eighteenth dynasty, see Egyptian chronology).","title":"Seqenenre Tao"},{"sentence_id":3,"text":" With his queen, Ahhotep I, Seqenenre Tao fathered two pharaohs, Kamose, his immediate successor who was the last pharaoh of the seventeenth dynasty, and Ahmose I who, following a regency by his mother, was the first pharaoh of the eighteenth.","title":"Seqenenre Tao"},{"sentence_id":4,"text":" Seqenenre Tao is credited with starting the opening moves in the war of liberation against the Hyksos, which was ended by his son Ahmose.","title":"Seqenenre Tao"},{"sentence_id":0,"text":"Hatshepsut ( ; also Hatchepsut; Egyptian: \"ḥ3.t-šps.wt\" \"Foremost of Noble Ladies\"; 1507–1458 BCE) was the fifth pharaoh of the Eighteenth Dynasty of Egypt.","title":"Hatshepsut"},{"sentence_id":1,"text":" She was the second historically confirmed female pharaoh, the first being Sobekneferu.","title":"Hatshepsut"},{"sentence_id":2,"text":" (Various other women may have also ruled as pharaohs regnant or at least regents before Hatshepsut, as early as Neithhotep around 1600 years prior.)","title":"Hatshepsut"},{"sentence_id":3,"text":" Hatshepsut came to the throne of Egypt in 1478 BCE.","title":"Hatshepsut"},{"sentence_id":4,"text":" Officially, she ruled jointly with Thutmose III, who had ascended to the throne the previous year as a child of about two years old.","title":"Hatshepsut"},{"sentence_id":5,"text":" Hatshepsut was the chief wife of Thutmose II, Thutmose III’s father.","title":"Hatshepsut"},{"sentence_id":6,"text":" She is generally regarded by Egyptologists as one of the most successful pharaohs, reigning longer than any other woman of an indigenous Egyptian dynasty.","title":"Hatshepsut"},{"sentence_id":7,"text":" According to Egyptologist James Henry Breasted she is also known as \"the first great woman in history of whom we are informed.\"","title":"Hatshepsut"},{"sentence_id":0,"text":"Meritaten, also spelled Merytaten or Meryetaten (14th century BC), was an ancient Egyptian queen of the Eighteenth dynasty, who held the position of Great Royal Wife to Pharaoh Smenkhkare, who may have been a brother or son of Akhenaten.","title":"Meritaten"},{"sentence_id":1,"text":" Her name means \"She who is beloved of Aten\"; Aten being the sun-god her father worshipped; Meritaten also may have served as pharaoh in her own right under the name, Ankhkheperure Neferneferuaten.","title":"Meritaten"},{"sentence_id":0,"text":"Nakhtmin (also Minnakht) held the position of generalissimo during the reign of pharaoh Tutankhamun of the Eighteenth Dynasty of Ancient Egypt.","title":"Nakhtmin"},{"sentence_id":1,"text":" His titles during the reign of Tutankhamun included \"the true servant who is beneficial to his lord, the king's scribe,\" \"the servant beloved of his lord,\" \"the Fan-bearer on the Right Side of the King,\" and \"the servant who causes to live the name of his lord.\"","title":"Nakhtmin"},{"sentence_id":2,"text":" These titles were found on five ushabtis that Nakhtmin offered as funerary presents for pharaoh Tutankhamun.","title":"Nakhtmin"},{"sentence_id":0,"text":"Parennefer also called Wennefer was a High Priest of Amun during the reigns of Tutankhamen and Horemheb (and possibly later).","title":"Parennefer called Wennefer"},{"sentence_id":1,"text":" He was previously thought to date to the time of Ramesses II, but he is now dated to the end of the Eighteenth Dynasty.","title":"Parennefer called Wennefer"},{"sentence_id":2,"text":" Parennefer was more firmly put at the end of the Eighteenth Dynasty after extensive excavations of his tomb in Thebes in 1990-1993.","title":"Parennefer called Wennefer"}],"peer_messages":[],"previous_answer":"noanswer","question":"Who was the First Prophert to the sixth Pharaoh of the Eighteenth Dynasty?"}
